item.title: Trump administration considers building baseball park in Grand Teton National Park that could host a Major League Baseball game
item.description: MLB approached the administration about hosting a game at a national park, officials from the White House and the league said. A senior official with the National Park Service scouted multiple locations in Grand Teton, according to two additional people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Dogs use a surprising method to understand human language, new study suggests
item.description: In a brain activity study, dogs seemed to listen for consonants to figure out when one word ends and another begins.

item.title: A horror story unfolds as police examine pornographer’s brutal trove
item.description: A Philadelphia man created hundreds of thousands of degrading images of women, police say. At least five may have been dead when they were photographed or recorded.

item.title: Democrats now have easier paths to flipping the Senate. Here are races to watch.
item.description: The goal of keeping Democratic Senate seats and flipping four held by Republicans once felt like a long shot. Now it seems feasible.

item.title: Lawmakers slam Trump’s move to cancel $810 million in funding approved by Congress
item.description: The White House announced plans to cancel funding for refugee services, climate change and other domestic programs. Lawmakers say it infringes on their spending authority.

item.title: U.S., Russia stripped human oversight from global AI weapons pact
item.description: The two nations weakened a range of safeguards in a landmark U.N. effort to try to regulate the use of lethal autonomous weaponry. The global negotiations this month marked the furthest progress yet toward a potential treaty.

item.title: White House blocks CNN from Trump’s scheduled trip to Tennessee on Air Force One
item.description: The decision puts the state of the rotational TV pool coverage of the president in jeopardy once again. CNN, along with MS NOW and Politico, was banned from White House grounds last week, but a federal judge temporarily restored access early Thursday. The five-network pool resumed coverage of Trump on Friday morning.

item.title: White House has not acted on RFK Jr.’s push for proof that ultra-processed foods are safe
item.description: A draft letter obtained by The Post shows Kennedy’s favorable response to a petition that food experts said could lead to significant changes for the industry.

item.title: Supreme Court again blocks Missouri congressional map favoring Republicans, ending legal fight that created major confusion
item.description: The justices on Friday said Missouri must instead use a map that will give Democrats a good shot at holding on to two of the state’s eight House seats. It was the third time this month that the Supreme Court has ruled against the GOP congressional map.

item.description: A stretch from New Jersey to Massachusetts could face significant coastal impacts beginning Friday night, with the storm moving northward and potentially pushing ashore Sunday. Rain and strong winds are expected all the way from the Carolinas to Maine.

item.title: Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson calls Supreme Court’s frequent use of emergency docket “problematic,” urges restraint
item.description: Speaking at the University of the District of Columbia, Jackson said the court has used the docket too often to issue decisions that have allowed the Trump administration to move forward while challenges play out in lower court. The emergency docket has been criticized by legal experts who say justices can make consequential decisions while offering little or no explanation for their reasoning.

item.title: Senate narrowly rejects measure to block Trump from ordering more strikes on Iran
item.description: Four Republicans joined Democrats in voting for it, while one Democrat opposed it. The administration ignored passage of a similar resolution in June, arguing that it lacks the force of law.

item.title: Trump-backed Nevada Republican exaggerated Bronze Star award in two campaigns
item.description: David Flippo, a Republican congressional candidate in Nevada, inflated his military record multiple times in recent years by claiming he received a Bronze Star “for valor” during his two-decade Air Force career. Flippo received a Bronze Star in 2004 for his service, but not the Bronze Star with valor, a much rarer distinction that recognizes heroism in direct combat with an enemy. Experts on military awards say such exaggerations are tantamount to lying.

item.title: California sheriff must return seized ballots, state Supreme Court rules
item.description: The court ruled unanimously that Chad Bianco lacked the authority to review the ballots based on a thin allegation of fraud stemming from a vote last year.

item.title: CNN and MS NOW journalists regain access to White House
item.description: Journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico had been blocked from the White House earlier Thursday by the U.S. Secret Service, despite a federal judge’s early-morning ruling that their access to the grounds be restored. Politico has not yet said if it was allowed back into the White House.

item.title: CNN, Politico and MS NOW request emergency court hearing as White House continues to deny them access
item.description: Some journalists from the news organizations were blocked from accessing the White House on Thursday despite a federal judge’s early-morning ruling ordering the Trump administration to restore their credentials. The judge gave the government until 12:30 p.m. to respond to the media outlets’ court filing alleging noncompliance with the order.

item.title: Trump dismantled U.S. climate policy. But his war on Iran is inadvertently cutting emissions.
item.description: While President Donald Trump remains a climate-change denier, the U.S. war with Iran has triggered an unforeseen benefit in the fight against global warming, leading to a plunge in the consumption of oil and gas around the world as fighting disrupts production and transportation.

A Politico reporter also had their press pass confiscated by the Secret Service and was blocked from entering White House grounds, the outlet reported.

Court records show that the five officers were all charged Wednesday with fraud and official misconduct.
